rule: Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings doctrine section coupling
description: `plugin/governance/remediation-doctrine.md` `## Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings` is the single source for how a user's rejection of a finding, and a threat model, persist across review runs. The source pin is the section heading. Four further pins in the same file carry the load-bearing claims. (1) The definition: a user's rejection of a finding and a threat model are decisions, each recorded at its source in the project's durable design record. (2) The key: the recorded decision, never a finding id or a question; rewriting the key back to a finding id or a per-run question turns the suite red. (3) The condition and its obligation in one span: a later finding that contests a recorded decision is a repeat, and the reviewer rejects it by citing the record, lists it for the user before the PR, does not fix it, and never asks again; deleting any one of those four obligations turns the suite red. The same span carries the boundary: a finding that shows a failure the record does not cover is new and gets First-Finding Triage. (4) The write obligation: when the user rejects a finding, the next plan records that decision at its source. The consumers pin the POINTER only, never remedy prose, so honest rewording of the doctrine body does not break them: `plugin/agents/local-reviewer.md`, `plugin/agents/github-reviewer.md` and `plugin/agents/overlord.md` must still name `## Recorded Decisions and Repeat Findings` in the doctrine file, and `plugin/agents/cerebrate.md` must still name it as the doctrine's section. What this pin honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in these five named files; it claims nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion that leaves the pinned bytes intact is invisible: surrounding prose that also lets a reviewer ask the user again, or that keys a decision on a finding id elsewhere, stays green; (2) the paragraph explaining why a finding id and a question cannot carry a decision is deliberately unpinned, so that the explanation stays cheap to reword honestly, and deleting it alone stays green; (3) the pin sees only the five files it names, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW reviewer that never points at the section at all, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

The key is the recorded decision, never a finding id or a question.

A later finding that contests a recorded decision is a REPEAT. The reviewer rejects it by citing the record, lists it for the user before the PR, does not fix it, and never asks again. A finding that shows a failure the record does not cover is NEW, and gets **First-Finding Triage**.
When the user rejects a finding, the next plan records that decision at its source, so the next review reads the record instead of asking again.
